rows.task_text: Identify the areas covered by exactly one of two polygon layers (an exterior-extent layer and a survey layer) — regions present in one layer but not in both. Output: a polygon layer of the non-overlapping areas. Any valid route to this result is acceptable.
rows.required_outcome: A polygon layer containing exactly the areas covered by one and only one of the two input polygon layers (symmetric difference / XOR of extent vs survey).
required_constraints: Two polygon inputs (exterior-extent layer, survey layer)
Output = polygons of non-overlapping areas
Any valid route is acceptable (stated in the task)
required_capabilities: Pairwise spatial overlay reasoning (what XOR means geometrically)
Producing a clean POLYGON result (geometry type matters)
acceptable_alternatives: XOR after prior dissolution to single parts
Line-based routes ONLY if they reliably rebuild the required polygon areas (conditional)
failure_conditions: Overlap (covered by both) appears in output
Result area deviates materially from true XOR
Output delivered as lines/points instead of polygons
rows.revision_note: R7: line-difference route made conditional (must rebuild polygon result)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'regions present in one layer but not in both'; 'Any valid route to this result is acceptable.'

rows.task_text: Generate a polygon layer of uniform-width bands tracing the boundaries of input polygons, for tactile-map edge rendering. The band width is user-specified and bands must be centred on the original outlines, free of geometry artefacts, and combined into a clean output. Output: polygon features representing the edge bands.
rows.required_outcome: A polygon layer of uniform-width bands tracing input polygon boundaries (tactile-map edge rendering).
required_constraints: Band width = user-specified TOTAL band width (not one-sided offset distance)
Bands centred on original outlines
Free of geometry artefacts
Bands combined into a clean output
acceptable_alternatives: Boundary extraction then buffer with cleanup — every route must deliver the SAME geometry semantics: total-width band centred on the outline
failure_conditions: Width used as one-sided offset (doubles total width)
Polygon interior filled instead of edge band
rows.revision_note: R7: width defined as TOTAL band width; alternative routes gated on identical geometry semantics
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'uniform-width bands … centred on the original outlines' — centring + uniform width fixes the total-width interpretation

rows.task_text: From a high-resolution DEM, produce three terrain-derivative rasters: slope in degrees, aspect in degrees, and a hillshade. The derivatives must be geometrically meaningful, which requires working in a projected metric CRS. Output: three georeferenced raster files added to the project.
rows.required_outcome: Three georeferenced terrain rasters: slope (degrees), aspect (degrees), hillshade.
required_constraints: Computation in projected metric CRS (geometric meaningfulness)
Slope/aspect in degrees
Hillshade produced (illumination parameters are free — the task does not require reporting them)
Three files added to project
acceptable_alternatives: Native-CRS-derive routes are NOT generally equivalent (derivatives depend on coordinate scale at computation time) — acceptable ONLY if the route demonstrably satisfies the task's projected-metric computation requirement
GDAL/GRASS/SAGA derivative families (any honoring the CRS requirement)
failure_conditions: NOTE: absence of reported illumination parameters is NOT a failure
rows.revision_note: R7: illumination-report requirement removed; native-CRS-derive route demoted from general equivalence to proof-required conditional
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'must be geometrically meaningful, which requires working in a projected metric CRS'; 'slope in degrees, aspect in degrees, and a hillshade' (no reporting requirement)

rows.task_text: Produce a per-municipality dominant drought-class map from a drought-severity polygon layer whose classes overlap. Overlaps must be resolved so that more severe classes take precedence (hierarchical exclusivity). For each municipality, determine the drought class covering the largest area within it. Output: (1) a municipality layer symbolized by dominant drought class and (2) a table listing each municipality's dominant class code/name and the corresponding area.
rows.required_outcome: (1) Municipality layer symbolized by dominant drought class; (2) table of municipality → dominant class code/name + area.
required_constraints: Overlapping severity classes resolved by hierarchical exclusivity (more severe takes precedence; original-text requirement)
Dominant = class covering the largest AREA within each municipality (area-based semantics)
Two outputs (map layer + table)
acceptable_alternatives: Sequential difference chain by severity order

Raster-based approaches ONLY if they explicitly compute or reliably approximate per-class area shares, with the accuracy/tolerance standard declared in advance (conditional; not an unconditional equivalent)
failure_conditions: Dominant class chosen wrongly (not largest area)
NOTE: class flips caused solely by raster resolution/boundary discretization are resolution artifacts — judged separately from semantic errors
rows.revision_note: R7-1: raster majority-vote removed as an unconditional equivalent; conditional with pre-declared area-accuracy standard; resolution artifacts separated from semantic errors
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'more severe classes take precedence (hierarchical exclusivity)' — verified as original-text requirement; 'drought class covering the largest area within it' — area semantics, not pixel votes

rows.task_text: From a vector layer, select the features whose string attribute matches a given case-insensitive pattern. Report (a) the total number of input features and (b) the number of matching features, and produce (c) the centroid of the matching features' merged geometry as a single point. Output: the matching features carrying both counts, and one centroid point feature carrying the same counts.
rows.required_outcome: Matching features carrying both counts + ONE centroid point feature carrying the same counts.
required_constraints: Case-insensitive pattern match on a string attribute
Count (a)=total input features, (b)=matching features
Point (c) = centroid of matching features' MERGED geometry
acceptable_alternatives: ANY construction acceptable as long as the result IS the single centroid of the merged matched-geometry set
failure_conditions: Counts wrong or attached to wrong layer
Centroid computed per-feature or on the unmatched set
underdetermined_aspects: Empty match set: task text does not define centroid/count-point behaviour — recorded as an undefined edge case; do not default to requiring a centroid
rows.revision_note: R7: construction freedom affirmed (result-semantic gating); empty-match edge case declared undefined
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'the centroid of the matching features' merged geometry as a single point'

rows.task_text: Map seafloor substrate units from ROV navigation tracks and annotations: for each annotated location, represent the area of seafloor visible to the camera as a substrate-classified polygon oriented along the track, then combine overlapping areas so each final unit carries a single substrate class. Output: a polygon layer of substrate mapping units with standardized styling.
rows.required_outcome: Polygon layer of seafloor substrate mapping units, each carrying a single substrate class, with standardized styling.
required_constraints: Inputs: ROV navigation tracks + annotations
Each annotated location's camera-visible area represented as substrate-classified polygon
Overlapping areas combined so each final unit has one class
Styled output
required_capabilities: Viewshed-like polygon construction consistent with camera coverage and track orientation
acceptable_alternatives: Wedge buffers oriented along track (matches original visibility semantics)
Other geometry constructions ONLY if they respect the task's camera-coverage and track-orientation definition
Sector/limited-rectangle approximations are directly equivalent ONLY if the original task explicitly endorses them (no such endorsement found → conditional, default NOT equivalent)
failure_conditions: Final units carry mixed substrate classes
Unit geometry unrelated to track/visibility semantics
underdetermined_aspects: Priority rule among overlapping DIFFERENT substrate classes is NOT defined by the task text — recorded UNDERDETERMINED; adjudication must not invent a priority (class-conflict outcomes are case-by-case, not automatic failures)
rows.revision_note: R7-2: geometry-approximation admission conditions stated; cross-class overlap priority declared UNDERDETERMINED (task text defines none; none invented)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'represent the area of seafloor visible to the camera as a substrate-classified polygon oriented along the track, then combine overlapping areas so each final unit carries a single substrate class'

rows.task_text: Merge small forest-stand polygons into adjacent, similar, larger stands. A small stand is eligible only when it touches a larger neighbour, the relative difference in dominant height stays within the given threshold, and the neighbour is of a qualifying type ('classified'). Each merged group must retain the attributes of its largest stand, and each output feature must state whether it was merged (merged = 1) or not (merged = 0). Output: a merged polygon layer.
rows.required_outcome: A merged polygon layer; each feature flagged merged=1/0; merged groups retain the largest stand's attributes.
required_constraints: Eligibility: touches a larger neighbour AND relative dominant-height difference within threshold AND neighbour type 'classified'
Every merge must satisfy the listed eligibility criteria
Attribute retention rule (largest stand per group)
Per-feature merged flag with defined semantics
acceptable_alternatives: Expression-based eligibility then dissolve by target id
ANY merge order/grouping in which every merge satisfies the eligibility criteria and the attribute rule — multiple valid final groupings are acceptable
failure_conditions: A merge violating any eligibility criterion
Attributes inherited from a smaller stand
NOTE: different valid merge orders yielding different (each valid) groupings are NOT failures
underdetermined_aspects: Exact 'relative difference' formula and tie-breaking among multiple qualifying neighbours are not fixed by the task text (threshold is data-given; formula delegates to data semantics) — multiple valid outcomes acceptable
rows.revision_note: R7: no formula/iteration-order/unique-path prescriptions; relative-difference formula and merge-order ties declared multiple-valid/underdetermined
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: three eligibility criteria verbatim; 'each output feature must state whether it was merged (merged = 1) or not (merged = 0)'

rows.task_text: Compute per-country mean values of several raster indicators using country boundaries as zones: land quality (one epoch) and population density for the years 1500, 1990, and 2000. Retain the country name and ISO code fields, attach one distinctly prefixed set of statistics per indicator epoch, and export the final attribute table as CSV. Output: a countries layer carrying all statistics, plus the exported CSV file.
rows.required_outcome: Countries layer carrying all statistics + exported CSV of the final attribute table.
required_constraints: Zones = country boundaries
Indicators: land quality (single epoch) + population density (1500, 1990, 2000)
Retain country name and ISO fields
Distinct prefix per indicator epoch
CSV export
acceptable_alternatives: Per-raster zonal stats then field merge
failure_conditions: Years attached to land quality or dropped from population density
CSV missing or schema inconsistent with layer
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'land quality (one epoch) and population density for the years 1500, 1990, and 2000'; 'distinctly prefixed set of statistics per indicator epoch'; 'export the final attribute table as CSV'

rows.task_text: Draw a representative sample of points from an input point layer based on the values of a numeric attribute. The sampling must support both a simple random mode and a stratified mode, in which the numeric field is first divided into classes (e.g., by quantiles or equal intervals) and points are sampled within each class. Output: a new point layer containing the sampled features with X and Y coordinate fields added.
rows.required_outcome: A new point layer with the sampled features, carrying X and Y coordinate fields.
required_constraints: Support simple random mode AND stratified mode
Strata derived from a numeric attribute (method flexible, e.g., quantiles/equal intervals)
Sampling occurs within each stratum
Output = subset of input points + X/Y coordinate fields
acceptable_alternatives: Quantile/equal-interval boundary computation then filtered selection
failure_conditions: Only simple random sampling implemented (stratified mode unsupported)
Classes ignored (sampling across strata rather than within)
Sample not a subset of input points
NOTE: sample size, ratio, per-stratum quotas, and 'representativeness' are UNDEFINED by the task text — they are NOT failure conditions and no threshold may be improvised
underdetermined_aspects: Sampling quantity/proportion/stratum quotas/random seed: unspecified in task text — unjudgeable by design
rows.revision_note: R7-3: failure conditions restricted to task-supported judgments; sample size/ratio/quotas declared undefined — representativeness never a failure
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'must support both a simple random mode and a stratified mode, in which the numeric field is first divided into classes (e.g., by quantiles or equal intervals)'

rows.task_text: Combine two polygon zoning layers (e.g., management zones and soil zones) into a single layer of non-overlapping atomic zones, where each output polygon represents a unique combination of the two zonings. The output must consist of valid single-part polygons, each uniquely identified. Output: one polygon layer with a unique zone ID and geometry attributes (area, perimeter) per zone.
rows.required_outcome: One polygon layer of non-overlapping atomic zones (unique combination of the two zonings), single-part, uniquely identified, with area/perimeter.
required_constraints: Each output polygon = unique combination of the two zonings
Valid single-part polygons
Unique zone ID
Geometry attributes (area, perimeter)
required_capabilities: Atomic-completeness awareness (all combinations present, none duplicated)
acceptable_alternatives: (Intersection + two differences) acceptable ONLY with a completeness verification that all atomic combinations are present with correct attributes (conditional)
REMOVED: 'intersect then symmetrical-difference cleanup' as an unconditional equivalent — it does not generally guarantee atomic completeness
failure_conditions: Zones not atomic (overlaps remain or combinations duplicated/missing)
rows.revision_note: R7-4: Intersect+SymDiff-cleanup route removed as unconditional equivalent; intersection+differences route made completeness-verification-conditional
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'each output polygon represents a unique combination of the two zonings'; 'must consist of valid single-part polygons, each uniquely identified'

rows.task_text: For a water-network vector layer restricted to a study area, produce results organized by the network's three hierarchical levels (Principal, Secundaria, Terciaria) according to the level attribute: one layer per level and a buffer zone around each level with its own specified radius (each level has a distinct radius). Output: the study-area network, one filtered layer per level, and one buffer layer per level.
rows.required_outcome: Study-area network + one filtered layer per level + one buffer layer per level.
required_constraints: Restrict to study area
Three levels (Principal, Secundaria, Terciaria) per level attribute
Each level buffered at its own distinct radius
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'three hierarchical levels (Principal, Secundaria, Terciaria) according to the level attribute'; 'each level has a distinct radius'; 'Output: the study-area network, one filtered layer per level, and one buffer layer per level'

rows.task_text: For each paddock polygon, produce a distance raster giving, for every location inside the paddock, the distance to the nearest water point located within that same paddock, in map units of the working CRS. Paddocks containing at least one water point each yield their own georeferenced distance raster named after the paddock; the set of per-paddock rasters is the final output — no additional summary statistic is required.
rows.required_outcome: One georeferenced distance raster per paddock (named after the paddock): for every location inside the paddock, distance to the nearest water point located within that same paddock.
required_constraints: Water points restricted to the SAME paddock (verified task semantics) — NOT bypassable
Distances in map units of the working CRS
Results spatially limited to the corresponding paddock extent
Only paddocks containing ≥1 water point produce output (task_text-defined)
The per-paddock raster set is the final output — no extra summary statistic
required_capabilities: Distance-field computation (rasterize→proximity OR vector distance field then rasterized — rasterization and clipping are common capabilities, NOT mandated steps)
acceptable_alternatives: Vector nearest-point distance field then rasterize
Any route honouring the distance semantics, per-paddock scoping, naming, and output-organization constraints
failure_conditions: Distance computed to GLOBAL nearest water point (violates inside-paddock semantics)
Units not map units / CRS inconsistent
Empty paddocks silently included or naming lost
Unrequested aggregation (max extraction etc.) presented as the deliverable
NOTE: different-but-reasonable resolution choices are NOT errors
underdetermined_aspects: Raster resolution, cell origin, and reference grid are unspecified by the task text — pixel-level comparison requires a separately declared alignment/tolerance rule (not improvised at scoring time)
rows.revision_note: R7-5: unspecified grid parameters (resolution/origin/reference grid) declared NOT hard scoring conditions; pixel-level comparison deferred to a separately declared alignment/tolerance rule; rasterize/clip demoted from mandated steps to common capabilities
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'distance to the nearest water point located within that same paddock, in map units of the working CRS'; original task_text defines output set 'one per paddock containing at least one water point'

rows.task_text: Assemble a natural-resource dataset for a specified property: obtain the relevant natural-resource features from the government feature service for the given lot/plan boundaries or extent, so that the final dataset covers exactly the target property area. Output: a single styled GeoPackage layer containing the property's natural-resource data.

Selection by lot/plan boundaries or given extent
Final DATA coverage restricted to the target property extent (interpretive note: features need not spatially fill the parcel — the dataset must be confined to it)
Single merged layer; GeoPackage; styled
failure_conditions: Data extends beyond the property extent or falls short of the selected lot/plan scope
Features unrelated to the property included

rows.evidence: task: 'so that the final dataset covers exactly the target property area' — read as a data-extent restriction (owner interpretive ruling), not a tessellation requirement

rows.task_text: For each polygon in an input layer, compute the area-weighted average of a numeric attribute from an overlay polygon layer, ensuring duplicated overlay geometry is not counted twice. Output: the input features with the area-weighted average attached, plus a report layer with per-feature details; a CRS check is expected for geographic or mismatched layers.
rows.required_outcome: Input features with area-weighted average attached + a report layer with per-feature details.
required_constraints: Weighting strictly by overlay fragment area
Duplicated overlay geometry (same geometry re-appearing) not counted twice; genuine overlaps between distinct overlay areas remain in the calculation
CRS check expected for geographic/mismatched layers
required_capabilities: Numeric consistency (weights sum to overlay area)
failure_conditions: Aggregation keyed wrongly (not per input feature)
NOTE: identical geometry carrying CONFLICTING numeric attribute values must NOT be resolved by implicit value choice — flagged case-by-case
underdetermined_aspects: Duplicate geometry with conflicting attribute values: weighted-average semantics become non-unique — recorded as adjudication cases, not auto-failures and not auto-merges
rows.revision_note: R7: duplicate-vs-overlap scope refined; conflicting-attribute duplicates declared adjudication cases (no implicit value choice)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task: 'area-weighted average … ensuring duplicated overlay geometry is not counted twice'; 'a report layer with per-feature details'

rows.task_text: Estimate noise levels (dBA) at receptor locations around a point noise source according to the BS 5228 standard, accounting for terrain between source and receptors, distance attenuation, ground type, and barriers. Input: a point source, receptor polygons, and a DEM; layers must be handled in a projected CRS. Output: a noise-level value per receptor and a styled source-point layer.
rows.required_outcome: A noise-level value (dBA) per receptor location + a styled source-point layer.
required_constraints: BS 5228 as the governing standard (hard semantic constraint)
Account for terrain (DEM), distance attenuation, ground type, and barriers
Inputs: point source, receptor polygons, DEM
Handle in projected CRS
acceptable_alternatives: Any implementation is acceptable ONLY if its resulting per-receptor noise estimates follow the applicable BS 5228 calculation requirements and account for terrain, distance attenuation, ground type, and barriers.
A generic viewshed analysis or arbitrary attenuation surface is NOT automatically compliant — route names never substitute for the standard's semantics
failure_conditions: Standard invoked by name while the plan's computation contradicts its requirements
underdetermined_aspects: Scoring boundary: from WORKFLOW STRUCTURE alone one can judge presence of source–receptor relationship, terrain factor, attenuation factors, and barrier handling; NUMERICAL BS 5228 compliance of computed values is NOT judgeable from structure alone (this PCA evaluates workflow plans, not executed numerics) — declared partial-scoring boundary
rows.revision_note: R7-6: BS 5228 semantic compliance is the hard constraint, not route names; structural vs domain-semantic scoring boundary declared
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2 (chain-consistency audit; gold authored independently of chains)
rows.evidence: task text (all five elements traced to original task sentences; see final_status §6 check#2)

Statistics attached to the ORIGINAL point locations

rows.revision_note: R7: statistic-set judgeability clarified — original enumeration cited as evidence; full-enumeration absence is NOT a hard failure against the frozen text
